It is run on this league and on other leagues of the same kind that you have not seen, so it has to learn\n9\teverything it needs from the league folder it is given.\n10\t\n11\t    python solution/forecast.py --league <folder> --out <file.csv>\n12\t\n13\tThe output file has two columns, `fixture` and `p_home`, with one row per fixture in `<folder>/fixtures.csv`.\n14\t\n15\t## How a forecast is graded\n16\t\n17\tThe league is simulated, so the [REDACTED] probability that the home side wins each fixture is known exactly. Your forecast is graded against\n18\tthat number. No match is played and no result is used, so luck has no part in the grade.\n19\t\n20\tFor a fixture with [REDACTED] probability `p` and forecast `q`, the penalty is `p*ln(p/q) + (1-p)*ln((1-p)/(1-q))`. It is zero when `q = p` and\n21\tgrows quickly when a forecast is confident and wrong. Forecasts are clipped to [0.002, 0.998]. Your regret on a league is the\n22\taverage penalty over its fixtures.\n23\t\n24\tYour regret is compared with that of a reference forecaster. The reference uses only the files you have, the engine you have, and standard\n25\tstatistical practice. It plays each fixture 4,000 times. Your program is run on this league and on seven leagues you have not seen. You pass\n26\tif your regret, summed over all eight leagues, is at most 10 percent above the reference's sum, and the same holds for the seven\n27\tunseen leagues on their own. Simulation noise in your own forecasts counts against you, so play each fixture enough times.\n28\t\n29\tFor orientation, summed over leagues like these a coin flip (0.5 everywhere) has a little under twice the reference's regret. On a single\n30\tleague anything can happen. Some leagues have little to predict, and there the reference itself can be close to the coin flip.\n31\t\n32\t## The files in a league folder\n33\t\n34\t| file | one row per | columns |\n35\t|---|---|---|\n36\t| `balls.csv` | legal ball | `season, match, innings, over, ball, batting_team, bowling_team, venue, batter, bowler, outcome, extra, position, wickets_before, runs_before, target` |\n37\t| `matches.csv` | match | `season, match, week, home, away, venue, toss_winner, batted_first, first_total, second_total, winner` |\n38\t| `lineups.csv` | player in a past match | `match, team, batting_slot, player, bowling_slot` |\n39\t| `players.csv` | player | `player, role, hand, bowling_style` |\n40\t| `venues.csv` | venue | `venue, home_team, pitch` |\n41\t| `fixtures.csv` | fixture to forecast | `fixture, season, home, away, venue` |\n42\t| `fixture_lineups.csv` | player in a fixture | `fixture, team, batting_slot, player, bowling_slot` |\n43\t\n44\t`outcome` is one of `W, 0, 1, 2, 4, 6`. `extra` is 1 when the ball also produced one extra run. `position` is the batter's place in the\n45\torder, from 0. `target` is 0 in the first innings. `bowling_slot` is -1 for players who do not bowl. `engine/league_io.py` reads a folder\n46\tinto the objects the engine uses.\n47\t\n48\t## How a ball works (all of this is public)\n49\t\n50\t`engine/model.py` is the engine, and `engine/public.json` holds its public constants. They are the exact definition; this section\n51\tdescribes them in words.\n52\t\n53\tEvery legal ball has six possible outcomes. Their probabilities come from a sum of effects on the log scale:\n54\t\n55\t1. a profile for the over being bowled (`over_logits`), a shift for the batter's position (`position_vectors`);\n56\t2. the match situation: how many more wickets have fallen than is usual at that over (`wickets_vector`), and in the second innings a\n57\t   constant shift plus the chase pressure, which is the log of the required run rate over the usual rate from that over on, clipped to\n58\t   [-1, 1.2] (`second_innings_vector`, `pressure_vector`, `par_rate`);\n59\t3. the batter's **style** and **quality**, the bowler's **type** and **quality**, and the **conditions**, each a single number that moves\n60\t   the six outcomes along a fixed public direction (`directions`).\n61\t\n62\tOn top of the ball, with a fixed probability one extra run is added (`extras_per_ball`). Batters bat in line-up order. The strike changes\n63\ton an odd number of runs and at the end of each over. The five bowlers bowl in rotation, one over each in turn. An innings ends after 120\n64\tlegal balls, ten wickets, or when the target is reached. The toss is a coin flip and the winner always chases. A tied match is settled by\n65\ta coin flip.\n66\t\n67\t## What is hidden, and how it is built\n68\t\n69\t* **Batters.** Style does not change. Quality is a fixed talent plus a form component that drifts slowly over months and is pulled back\n70\t  toward zero. A batter's quality can differ a little against pace and against spin. Every player bats, so every player has these values.\n71\t* **Bowlers.** Type is related to the public bowling style and does not change. Quality is talent plus slowly drifting form.\n72\t* **Conditions.** A level for each venue; a league-wide level that moves from season to season and keeps moving; a pitch-on-the-day\n73\t  effect drawn afresh for every match and shared by both innings; dew at some venues, which helps the chase; a small general\n74\t  disadvantage for the side batting second; a lift for batters at their home ground; a personal liking of each batter for each venue;\n75\t  small league-wide effects of batting hand against bowling style and of pitch type on bowling style.\n76\t* There is **no** effect that belongs to one specific batter against one specific bowler.\n77\t* Between seasons about a quarter of the players change teams, and line-ups rotate heavily from match to match.\n78\t\n79\tThe fixtures are played at the start of the next season. Fix your random seeds.\n86\t* It has 12 minutes per league on two CPU cores and must not use the network.\n87\t* The engine is yours to use in any way you like, including to test your own method on leagues you simulate yourself.\n88\t\n89\t## Source\n90\t\n91\tCalibration constants derived from data sourced from Cricsheet (cricsheet.org), licensed under the Open Data Commons Attribution License\n92\t(ODC-BY 1.0). a wicket scores nothing\n8\tRUNS = np.array([0, 0, 1, 2, 4, 6])\n9\t# the two bowling styles, as integers so they can index tables\n10\tPACE, SPIN = 0, 1\n11\t\n12\t@dataclass\n13\tclass PlayerTable:\n14\t    # one entry per player in the league, indexed by player id; these are public facts about a player\n15\t    role: np.ndarray\n16\t    hand: np.ndarray # 0 right, 1 left\n17\t    style: np.ndarray # PACE or SPIN; meaningful only for players who bowl\n18\t\n19\t@dataclass\n20\tclass VenueTable:\n21\t    # one entry per ground, indexed by venue id; also public\n22\t    home_team: np.ndarray\n23\t    pitch: np.ndarray # 0 neutral, 1 helps pace, 2 helps spin\n24\t\n25\t@dataclass\n26\tclass Fixture:\n27\t    # one match's line-ups: the eleven and the five bowlers for each side, plus where and when it is played\n28\t    match: int\n29\t    season: int\n30\t    home: int\n31\t    away: int\n32\t    venue: int\n33\t    home_xi: np.ndarray\n34\t    home_bowlers: np.ndarray\n35\t    away_xi: np.ndarray\n36\t    away_bowlers: np.ndarray\n37\t\n38\t@dataclass\n39\tclass History:\n40\t    # everything an AI agent is allowed to see about the past: every ball, every match, the players, the grounds, the line-ups\n41\t    balls: pd.DataFrame\n42\t    matches: pd.DataFrame\n43\t    players: PlayerTable\n44\t    venues: VenueTable\n45\t    played: list = field(default_factory = list) # the Fixture of every past match (who played, who bowled)\n46\t    seasons: int = 0\n47\t\n48\t@dataclass\n49\tclass BattingCard:\n50\t    # what the innings simulator needs about the eleven batters of one side in one match; built by SkillBook.cards\n51\t    style: np.ndarray        \n52\t    quality: np.ndarray      \n53\t    conditions: np.ndarray   # (11, 5): venue affinity, home lift, hand-by-style and pitch effects for each batter-bowler meeting\n54\t\n55\t@dataclass\n56\tclass BowlingCard:\n57\t    # the same for the five bowlers of the other side\n58\t    kind: np.ndarray\n59\t    quality: np.ndarray\n60\t\n61\tclass BallModel:\n62\t    # Public part of a ball. Holds the measured constants and the five directions; adds up the situation. Nothing hidden lives here.\n63\t    def __init__(self, cal):\n64\t        self.cal = cal\n65\t        d = cal.directions\n66\t        # short names for the five unit vectors: batter style, batter quality, bowler type, bowler quality, conditions\n67\t        self.bs = d[\"bat_style\"]\n68\t        self.bq = d[\"bat_quality\"]\n69\t        self.wt = d[\"bowl_type\"]\n70\t        self.wq = d[\"bowl_quality\"]\n71\t        self.c = d[\"conditions\"]\n72\t\n73\t    def pressure(self, target, runs, ball):\n74\t        # chase pressure, the same formula as in the fit: log of the rate still needed over the rate sides usually maange from here.\n75\t        # `ball` counts legal balls from 0 to 119, so (120 - ball) / 6 is the overs left. Clipped so freak situations do not dominate.\n76\t        need = np.clip(target - runs, 1, None) / ((120 - ball) / 6)\n77\t        return np.clip(np.log(need / self.cal.par_rate[ball // 6]), -1.0, 1.2)\n78\t\n79\t    def situation(self, over, position, wickets, chasing, pressure):\n80\t        \"\"\"\n81\t        The public part of the logits: the over, the batting position and the match situation. Works for one ball or a table of balls.\n82\t        \"\"\"\n83\t        # each term is one effect from the fitted model\n84\t        # np.multiply.outer scales a six-vector by one number per ball\n85\t        cal = self.cal\n86\t        z = cal.over_logits[over] + cal.position_vectors[position] + np.multiply.outer(wickets - cal.typical_wickets[over], cal.wickets_vector)\n87\t        return z + np.multiply.outer(chasing, cal.second_innings_vector) + np.multiply.outer(pressure, cal.pressure_vector)\n88\t\n89\t    @staticmethod\n90\t    def shares(z):\n91\t        # six scores become six probabilities; subtracting the row maximum changes nothing and stops exp() overflowing\n92\t        p = np.exp(z - z.max(axis=1, keepdims=True))\n93\t        return p / p.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)\n94\t\n95\t# Innings Simulator\n96\tclass InningsSimulator:\n97\t    # Plays many copies of one innings at once. Every array below would have one entry per copy, so a ball is one vectorized step.\n98\t    def __init__(self, model):\n99\t        self.model = model\n100\t\n101\t    def play(self, batting, bowling, conditions, n, gen, target = None, log = None):\n102\t        \"\"\"\n103\t        Plays n copies of one innings and returns the n totals.\n104\t        `conditions` is a number of one value per copy.\n105\t        \"\"\"\n106\t        m, rows = self.model, np.arange(n)\n107\t        # who is on strike, who is at the other end, and who comes in next, as positions 0 to 10 in batting order\n108\t        striker, partner, next_in = np.zeros(n, int), np.ones(n, int), np.full(n, 2)\n109\t        # wickets lost, runs scored, and whether this copy's innings is still going\n110\t        wickets = np.zeros(n, int)\n111\t        runs = np.zeros(n, int)\n112\t        live = np.ones(n, bool)\n113\t        chasing = 0.0 if target is None else 1.0\n114\t        for ball in range(120):\n115\t            over = ball // 6\n116\t            # five bowlers rotate over by over; a bowler never bowls two overs in a row\n117\t            who = over % 5\n118\t            pressure = 0.0 if target is None else m.pressure(target, runs, ball)\n119\t            # the public part of the six scores, then the hidden numbers of the striker, the bowler and the conditions, each along its direction\n120\t            z = m.situation(over, striker, wickets, np.full(n, chasing), pressure)\n121\t            z = z + np.outer(batting.style[striker], m.bs) + np.outer(batting.quality[striker, who], m.bq)\n122\t            z = z + bowling.kind[who] * m.wt + bowling.quality[who] * m.wq + np.outer(conditions + batting.conditions[striker, who], m.c)\n123\t            p = m.shares(z)\n124\t            # one uniform draw per copy picks the outcome from the cumulative probabilities; the minimum guards against rounding\n125\t            kind = np.minimum((gen.random(n)[:, None] > p.cumsum(axis=1)).sum(axis=1), 5)\n126\t            # an extra run with the measured probability, independent of the bat outcome\n127\t            extra = (gen.random(n) < m.cal.extras_per_ball) & live\n128\t            # optional ball-by-ball record of copy 0, used by the league to write the history files\n129\t            if log is not None and live[0]:\n130\t                log.append((ball, int(striker[0]), who, int(kind[0]), int(extra[0]), int(wickets[0]), int(runs[0])))\n131\t            out = (kind == 0) & live\n132\t            scored = np.where(live & ~out, RUNS[kind], 0)\n133\t            runs += scored + extra\n134\t            wickets += out\n135\t            # the next batter replaces a dismissed striker\n136\t            striker = np.where(out, next_in, striker)\n137\t            next_in = next_in + out\n138\t            # the batters cross on an odd number of runs and at the end of an over, but not both\n139\t            swap = (scored % 2 == 1) ^ (ball % 6 == 5)\n140\t            striker, partner = np.where(swap, partner, striker), np.where(swap, striker, partner)\n141\t            # after the tenth wicket the indices would run past the eleven; clamp them, the innings is over anyway\n142\t            striker, partner = np.minimum(striker, 10), np.minimum(partner, 10)\n143\t            # an innings ends at ten wickets, or when a chase reaches its target\n144\t            live &= wickets < 10\n145\t            if target is not None:\n146\t                live &= runs < target\n147\t        return runs\n148\t\n149\tclass SkillBook:\n150\t    \"\"\"Everything the engine needs to know about players and venues. \n151\t    The league owns the [REDACTED] one. Per player-venue: affinity. Whole league: home lift, era (season level), day spread, wear.\n155\t    # Two small public-structure tables: type_table [hand][bowling style] and pitch_table [bowling style][pitch type].\n156\t\n157\t    def __init__(self, players, venues, style, quality, split, kind, bowl_quality, type_table, pitch_table, venue_level, venue_dew, affinity, home_lift, era, day_sd, wear):\n158\t        self.players, self.venues = players, venues\n159\t        self.style, self.quality, self.split, self.kind, self.bowl_quality = style, quality, split, kind, bowl_quality\n160\t        self.type_table, self.pitch_table = np.asarray(type_table), np.asarray(pitch_table)\n161\t        self.venue_level, self.venue_dew, self.affinity = venue_level, venue_dew, affinity\n162\t        self.home_lift, self.era, self.day_sd, self.wear = home_lift, era, day_sd, wear\n163\t\n164\t    def cards(self, xi, team, bowlers, venue):\n165\t        # builds the two cards for one side batting against five named bowlers at one ground\n166\t        hand, how = self.players.hand[xi], self.players.style[bowlers]\n167\t        # a batter's quality against pace is quality + split/2, against spin quality - split/2\n168\t        sign = np.where(how == PACE, 0.5, -0.5)\n169\t        at_home = self.home_lift if self.venues.home_team[venue] == team else 0.0\n170\t        # the conditions each batter meets against each bowler: liking for the ground, home lift, hand-versus-style, and the pitch's help to that style\n171\t        meeting = (self.affinity[xi, venue] + at_home)[:, None] + self.type_table[hand][:, how] - self.pitch_table[how, self.venues.pitch[venue]][None, :]\n172\t        batting = BattingCard(self.style[xi], self.quality[xi][:, None] + self.split[xi][:, None] * sign[None, :], meeting + self.pair_effect(xi, bowlers))\n173\t        return batting, BowlingCard(self.kind[bowlers], self.bowl_quality[bowlers])\n174\t\n175\t    def pair_effect(self, xi, bowlers):\n176\t        # a forecaster that believes in head-to-head records can override this; the [REDACTED] league has none\n177\t        return 0.0                       # the [REDACTED] league has no effect tied to one specific batter-bowler pair\n178\t\n179\t    def shift(self, venue, chasing):\n180\t        # the conditions shared by every ball of an innings: the ground's level, the season level, and in a chase the dew minus the wear\n181\t        return self.venue_level[venue] + self.era + ((self.venue_dew[venue] - self.wear) if chasing else 0.0)\n182\t\n183\t\n184\tclass MatchSimulator:\n185\t    def __init__(self, model):\n186\t        self.innings = InningsSimulator(model)\n187\t\n188\t    def win_probability(self, book, fixture, n, gen):\n189\t        \"\"\"\n190\t        P(home side wins). \n191\t        The toss is a coin flip and the winner always chases. \n192\t        A tie is settled by a coin flip.\n193\t        \"\"\"\n194\t        f = fixture\n195\t        xi, five = {f.home: f.home_xi, f.away: f.away_xi}, {f.home: f.home_bowlers, f.away: f.away_bowlers}\n196\t        total = 0.0\n197\t        # both orders of batting are played, each with weight one half, because the toss decides who chases\n198\t        for first, second in ((f.home, f.away), (f.away, f.home)):\n199\t            day = gen.normal(0.0, book.day_sd, n) if book.day_sd > 0 else np.zeros(n)       # the same pitch for both innings of a copy\n200\t            set_ = self.innings.play(*book.cards(xi[first], first, five[second], f.venue), book.shift(f.venue, False) + day, n, gen)\n201\t            chase = self.innings.play(*book.cards(xi[second], second, five[first], f.venue), book.shift(f.venue, True) + day, n, gen, target=set_ + 1)\n202\t            # one entry per player in the league, indexed by player id; these are public facts about a player\n    role: np.ndarray\n    hand: np.ndarray # 0 right, 1 left\n    style: np.ndarray # PACE or SPIN; meaningful only for players who bowl\n\n@dataclass\nclass VenueTable:\n    # one entry per ground, indexed by venue id; also public\n    home_team: np.ndarray\n    pitch: np.ndarray # 0 neutral, 1 helps pace, 2 helps spin\n\n@dataclass\nclass Fixture:\n    # one match's line-ups: the eleven and the five bowlers for each side, plus where and when it is played\n    match: int\n    season: int\n    home: int\n    away: int\n    venue: int\n    home_xi: np.ndarray\n    home_bowlers: np.ndarray\n    away_xi: np.ndarray\n    away_bowlers: np.ndarray\n\n@dataclass\nclass History:\n    # the Fixture of every past match (who played, who bowled)\n    seasons: int = 0\n\n@dataclass\nclass BattingCard:\n    # what the innings simulator needs about the eleven batters of one side in one match; built by SkillBook.cards\n    style: np.ndarray        \n    quality: np.ndarray      \n    conditions: np.ndarray   # Works for one ball or a table of balls.\n        \"\"\"\n        # each term is one effect from the fitted model\n        # np.multiply.outer scales a six-vector by one number per ball\n        cal = self.cal\n        z = cal.over_logits[over] + cal.position_vectors[position] + np.multiply.outer(wickets - cal.typical_wickets[over], cal.wickets_vector)\n        return z + np.multiply.outer(chasing, cal.second_innings_vector) + np.multiply.outer(pressure, cal.pressure_vector)\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def shares(z):\n        # six scores become six probabilities; subtracting the row maximum changes nothing and stops exp() overflowing\n        p = np.exp(z - z.max(axis=1, keepdims=True))\n        return p / p.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)\n\n# Innings Simulator\nclass InningsSimulator:\n    # Plays many copies of one innings at once. a bowler never bowls two overs in a row\n            who = over % 5\n            pressure = 0.0 if target is None else m.pressure(target, runs, ball)\n            # the public part of the six scores, then the hidden numbers of the striker, the bowler and the conditions, each along its direction\n            z = m.situation(over, striker, wickets, np.full(n, chasing), pressure)\n            z = z + np.outer(batting.style[striker], m.bs) + np.outer(batting.quality[striker, who], m.bq)\n            z = z + bowling.kind[who] * m.wt + bowling.quality[who] * m.wq + np.outer(conditions + batting.conditions[striker, who], m.c)\n            p = m.shares(z)\n            # one uniform draw per copy picks the outcome from the cumulative probabilities; the minimum guards against rounding\n            kind = np.minimum((gen.random(n)[:, None] > p.cumsum(axis=1)).sum(axis=1), 5)\n            # an extra run with the measured probability, independent of the bat outcome\n            extra = (gen.random(n) < m.cal.extras_per_ball) & live\n            # optional ball-by-ball record of copy 0, used by the league to write the history files\n            if log is not None and live[0]:\n                log.append((ball, int(striker[0]), who, int(kind[0]), int(extra[0]), int(wickets[0]), int(runs[0])))\n            out = (kind == 0) & live\n            scored = np.where(live & ~out, RUNS[kind], 0)\n            runs += scored + extra\n            wickets += out\n            # the next batter replaces a dismissed striker\n            striker = np.where(out, next_in, striker)\n            next_in = next_in + out\n            # the batters cross on an odd number of runs and at the end of an over, but not both\n            swap = (scored % 2 == 1) ^ (ball % 6 == 5)\n            striker, partner = np.where(swap, partner, striker), np.where(swap, striker, partner)\n            # after the tenth wicket the indices would run past the eleven; the [REDACTED] league has none\n        return 0.0                       # the [REDACTED] league has no effect tied to one specific batter-bowler pair\n\n    def shift(self, venue, chasing):\n        # the conditions shared by every ball of an innings: the ground's level, the season level, and in a chase the dew minus the wear\n        return self.venue_level[venue] + self.era + ((self.venue_dew[venue] - self.wear) if chasing else 0.0)\n\n\nclass MatchSimulator:\n    def __init__(self, model):\n        self.innings = InningsSimulator(model)\n\n    def win_probability(self, book, fixture, n, gen):\n        \"\"\"\n        P(home side wins). \n        The toss is a coin flip and the winner always chases. \n        A tie is settled by a coin flip.\n        \"\"\"\n        f = fixture\n        xi, five = {f.home: f.home_xi, f.away: f.away_xi}, {f.home: f.home_bowlers, f.away: f.away_bowlers}\n        total = 0.0\n        # both orders of batting are played, each with weight one half, because the toss decides who chases\n        for first, second in ((f.home, f.away), (f.away, f.home)):\n            day = gen.normal(0.0, book.day_sd, n) if book.day_sd > 0 else np.zeros(n)       # the same pitch for both innings of a copy\n            set_ = self.innings.play(*book.cards(xi[first], first, five[second], f.venue), book.shift(f.venue, False) + day, n, gen)\n            chase = self.innings.play(*book.cards(xi[second], second, five[first], f.venue), book.shift(f.venue, True) + day, n, gen, target=set_ + 1)\n            # the chasing side wins if it passes the total; a tie is worth half\n            second_wins = (chase > set_).mean() + 0.5 * (chase == set_).mean()\n            total += 0.5 * (second_wins if second == f.home else 1 - second_wins)\n        return float(total)\n\n\nclass PublicConstants:\n    \"\"\"\n    The documented structure of a ball: \n        everything in the engine that is not a hidden skill or a hidden condition.\n    \"\"\"\n    # This is what ships to the agent as public.json: the profiles, the situation responses, the directions and the extras rate.\n    # The spreads, the venue spread and the real targets from calibration.json are deliberately not in it.\n    FIELDS = (\"over_logits\", \"position_vectors\", \"wickets_vector\", \"pressure_vector\", \"second_innings_vector\", \"typical_wickets\", \"par_rate\")\n\n    def __init__(self, raw):\n        for name in self.FIELDS:\n            setattr(self, name, np.array(raw[name]))\n        self.directions = {k: np.array(v) for k, v in raw[\"directions\"].items()}\n        self.extras_per_ball = raw[\"extras_per_ball\"]\n\n    @classmethod\n    def from_calibration(cls, cal):\n        raw = {name: getattr(cal, name).tolist() for name in cls.FIELDS}\n        raw.update(directions={k: v.tolist() for k, v in cal.directions.items()}, extras_per_ball=cal.extras_per_ball)\n        return raw\n\n\ndef load_public_model(path=None):\n    # what the AI agent's copy of the engine does: build a BallModel from public.json beside it\n    raw = json.loads(Path(path or Path(__file__).with_name(\"public.json\")).read_text())\n    return BallModel(PublicConstants(raw))","numLines":233,"startLine":1,"totalLines":233}}}

def unpack(theta):\n        return {name: theta[offsets[name][0]:offsets[name][1]] for name in offsets}\n\n    def loss_and_grad(theta):\n        p_ = unpack(theta)\n        bs_p = p_[\"bs_p\"]\n vl[venue_id]\n            + era_s[season]\n            + hl * is_home_bat\n            + type_tab[hand, bstyle]\n            - pitch_tab[bstyle, pitch]\n            + chasing * (vd[venue_id] - wear)\n g_wear = np.array([-(d_c * chasing).sum()])\n        idx_type = hand * 2 + bstyle\n        g_type = np.bincount(idx_type, weights=d_c, minlength=4)\n        idx_pitch = bstyle * 3 + pitch\n balls.over.to_numpy(np.int64)\n    ball_in_over = balls.ball.to_numpy(np.int64)\n    position = balls.position.to_numpy(np.int64)\n    wickets = balls.wickets_before.to_numpy(np.int64)\n    runs = balls.runs_before.to_numpy(np.int64)\n    target = balls.target.to_numpy(np.int64)\n    innings = balls.innings.to_numpy(np.int64)\n    bat = balls.batter.to_numpy(np.int64)\n    bowler = balls.bowler.to_numpy(np.int64)\n    venue_id = balls.venue.to_numpy(np.int64)\n    batting_team = balls.batting_team.to_numpy(np.int64)\n    outcome = balls.outcome.to_numpy(np.int64)\n    season = balls.season.to_numpy(np.int64)\n\n    N = len(balls)\n    chasing = (innings == 2).astype(np.float64)\n    ball_num = 6 * over + ball_in_over\n\n    pressure = np.zeros(N)\n    mask = target > 0\n    if mask.any():\n        need = np.clip(target[mask] - runs[mask], 1, None) / ((120 - ball_num[mask]) / 6.0)\n        pressure[mask] = np.clip(np.log(need / cal.par_rate[over[mask]]), -1.0, 1.2)\n\n
